task:
REVISE THE F4 DESIGN DOC FOR THREE FOLLOW-UP REVIEW FINDINGS (PR #801). Target branch codex/run-38015883683-1, expected head 10bedd3; fail closed and write nothing if it moved. Only docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-10-v3-finder-f4-archetype-ui-design.md may change. Verify claims against the code (cite file:line); extend 'Review dispositions (2026-10-10)' with items 16-18.

16. (P1, ~line 851) 'Bound scans before applying non-indexed filters': non-indexed predicates (region, distance, ELW counts, etc. from the joined system_search row) applied before the 10,000 limit let PostgreSQL inspect nearly the whole archetype population. CHANGE slice 1c so the candidate window is taken FIRST from the index (generation, archetype_key, archetype_score DESC, system_id64) — the first 10,000 rows in raw-score order with no other predicate — and ALL other filters (min score excepted, since score is in the index) are applied within that window; the capped count is the count within the window after filtering; the UI copy becomes 'filters applied within the top 10,000 by <archetype> score' and the truncation flag reflects the window, not the filtered population. State that this guarantees a bounded scan for every selected request regardless of filters, and that offering broader filtered selected searches later would require new access paths (name them as a deferred option).

17. (P2, ~line 727) 'Choose a fixture archetype that admits all three rows': the specified Manufacturing Hub B-floor journey cannot traverse three pages — HD 38179 (Refinery 0 / Industrial 65) gets a Manufacturing Hub core of ~13 and cannot reach 60. CHANGE: compute, from the committed fixture (tests/fixtures/cypress_v3_sources via scripts/dev/seed_cypress_v3_generation.py and scripts/v3_system_archetype_model.py — actually run the model over the three fixture systems' vectors or reason from their economy potentials with citations), which archetype/floor combination yields a score >= the chosen floor for all three systems; specify that journey (archetype, min tier, expected order) in the E2E section, or, if no archetype admits all three at B, specify the journey at min tier C/D explicitly for the fixture lane only (the gate/bound rules from disposition 14 still apply) — and say which you chose and why.

18. (P1, ~line 854) 'Version the new candidate-window ranking semantics': the two-stage window changes the ranking definition, but ranking/profile.py's PROFILE_SPEC / v3-colony-potential-1 hash is not in the slice 1c file list. CHANGE: add apps/api/src/ranking/profile.py (and its tests) to slice 1c's exact file list, state that PROFILE_SPEC gains the candidate-window rule (window size, raw-score order, within-window modifier, capped count) and that the ranking identity is bumped (v3-colony-potential-2) so responses advertise an identity that reproduces the results; note the drift-guard test must be updated to the new recorded hash.

Validation: git diff --name-only origin/main lists only the design doc; Markdown renders. Commit message: 'docs(finder): F4 design — index-first candidate window, fixture-admitting E2E journey, versioned ranking semantics'.
